tagline: Hayfields and border lakes spread beyond the turnouts on US 1
intro: The Million Dollar View Scenic Byway follows US 1, with scenic turnouts overlooking rolling hayfields, lakes and the landscape of New Brunswick. The National Scenic Byway Foundation identifies it as an eight-mile state byway and highlights views of East Grand, Brackett and Deering lakes, Mount Katahdin and Peekaboo Mountain.

Weston was incorporated in 1835. The lakes have an older collective name, Shoodic, and belong to the Chiputneticook chain at the headwaters of the St. Croix River. The international boundary passes through East Grand Lake itself.

For a southbound journey, Orient comes before Weston, its neighbor to the south. The turnouts on US 1 give views across the lakes and hayfields; East Grand stretches for 22 miles. Continuing south leads toward Danforth village, where US 1 passes along the eastern side.

moments.title: Orient
moments.text: Orient’s eastern edge follows the Saint Croix River beside North Lake parish in New Brunswick. The Orient–Fosterville Border Crossing connects the two. Weston lies to the south, the next town in this southbound sequence.

moments.title: Weston
moments.text: Weston’s town boundary takes in 9.94 square miles of water out of a total 40.55 square miles, figures reported by the United States Census Bureau. The town was incorporated in 1835 and had 245 residents at the 2020 census.

moments.title: East Grand Lake
moments.text: The international boundary runs through East Grand Lake, dividing water shared by Maine and New Brunswick. The lake reaches 22 miles in length and four miles at its widest point. It belongs to the Chiputneticook chain, whose lakes form the headwaters of the St. Croix River. Its water level is controlled by the Forest City Dam in New Brunswick. Landlocked salmon, lake trout, smallmouth bass and American eel are among the species living here. The Maine shore belongs to Washington and Aroostook counties; across the boundary, the lake forms the western edge of New Brunswick’s York County.
